endorsements.quote: All hardware and software components used within DP systems must comply with applicable legal and regulatory requirements.
Every pathology laboratory intending to use DP for primary diagnosis must conduct its own validation study.

Significant technical changes—such as the introduction of new scanners, monitors, or software versions—require revalidation, the scope of which should correspond to the extent and nature of the implemented changes.
All connections should be encrypted using the TLS protocol, and two-factor authentication is strongly recommended to enhance access control.
Data must be stored and processed exclusively within the territory of the European Union, in full compliance with applicable data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR).

unlisted_practices: Perform regular calibration, preventive servicing, and documented maintenance of slide scanners according to manufacturer recommendations.

Establish regular, documented image quality control procedures for whole slide imaging, and investigate and resolve the root cause of any quality irregularity before returning the system to clinical operation.
Use open, non-proprietary image formats and interoperability standards such as DICOM and HL7 for integrating digital pathology systems with the laboratory and hospital information systems.
Implement barcode readability verification and automated linkage between physical slides and digital images to prevent mislinked specimen data.

Conduct pathologist-led validation of digital diagnosis by comparing digital and glass slide diagnoses, documenting discordances, and archiving a signed validation protocol before independent digital diagnosis.
Retain digital slides for at least six months, with about two years optimal, and archive glass slides according to legal retention requirements.
Avoid relying on a single scanner in routine diagnostics, and provide a backup telepathology system for intraoperative consultations.
Perform daily pre-use checks of scanners, network connectivity, and remote viewing platforms for intraoperative digital pathology.
Regularly update digital pathology recommendations in line with the latest professional standards.
Ensure cloud platforms used for digital pathology allow export of images to local storage and support high availability and resilience.
